title: Bishop Score
sources: Bishop EH. Pelvic scoring for elective induction. Obstet Gynecol. 1964;24:266-268.
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 107: Induction of Labor. Obstet Gynecol. 2009 (reaffirmed).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Obstetric/Newborn calculators existed only via the peds-module APGAR cross-list into this category).

purpose: Estimates cervical readiness for labor induction from the bedside cervical exam — a favorable score predicts a vaginal-delivery success rate similar to spontaneous labor.

interpretation.label: Unfavorable
interpretation.risk: Higher induction-failure and cesarean risk — cervical ripening (prostaglandin or mechanical) before oxytocin is usually indicated

interpretation.label: Intermediate
interpretation.risk: Borderline — ripening agents are still reasonable depending on the full clinical picture

interpretation.label: Favorable
interpretation.risk: Vaginal-delivery success rate similar to spontaneous labor — oxytocin induction alone is reasonable

notes: The classic cutoff is ≥ 8 = favorable, ≤ 6 = unfavorable; some protocols use < 6 rather than ≤ 6 as the unfavorable threshold — check your local induction protocol. A modified 3-component version (dilation, effacement, station only) is sometimes used and correlates well, but the full 5-component score is what's validated and reported in the original literature.
buildNote: Standard additive engine, 5 items summing to 0-13.
